title: Depth: conventions and core's depth nodes
hook: Which end is white, what the grey steps mean, and which depth nodes core really has: Lotus, MoGe and Depth Anything 3, read from the source.

verified.claim: The lab's v2_style, min_max and disparity give the same values as the real functions on a test ramp, difference 0.0.
All three renders put near at the bright end.
DA3Render's normalization choices are v2_style, min_max and raw, and raw is neither scaled nor clamped.
MoGeRender's depth is 1/depth, cut at the 0.1 and 99.9 percentiles.
Core's Lotus node has no inputs and returns a fixed conditioning. Core's Lotus blueprint runs one step with SetFirstSigma 999 and ends in ImageInvert.
ControlNet 1.1's depth model was trained on Midas, Leres and Zoe depth at three resolutions, and the page states no near or far convention.

unchecked: We ran no depth model and no depth ControlNet for this lesson. All numbers are from a synthetic ramp.
Near-is-white for the common SD 1.5 depth ControlNets is what the graph note and common practice assume. The model's own page does not state it, so check with one render.
Whether the Lotus blueprint's result before ImageInvert is far-is-white is an inference from the invert, not a run.
